title: Optimal AVR cycle count for a PRIDE linear layer
summary: Decide whether a PRIDE-compatible 64-bit linear layer can beat the source's 36-cycle AVR implementation benchmark.

formal_statement.body: In the Section 5.1 AVR instruction and register model of the PRIDE source, consider every 64-bit binary linear layer satisfying the source's linear- and differential-branch-number-four and full-dependency requirements. Determine the exact minimum cycle count. In particular, construct a conforming implementation using at most 35 cycles, or prove that every conforming implementation requires at least 36 cycles; the source's restricted interleaving construction supplies a 36-cycle implementation.

scope.domain: Software implementation optimization of symmetric block-cipher linear layers in the source-defined AVR model
assumptions: The target instruction set, register semantics, and scalar cycle costs are those fixed in Section 5.1.
The complete linear layer acts on 64 bits and has the source's branch number four and full-dependency properties.
The comparison class includes layers outside the interleaving construction used for the source benchmark.
scope.unresolved_remainder: It is unknown whether any admissible 64-bit layer outside the source's interleaving search space has an implementation below 36 AVR cycles, or whether 36 is a global optimum in the fixed model.

provenance.note: The exact benchmark and the question about the reduced search space are stated in the CRYPTO 2014 source.

citations.label: Albrecht--Driessen--Kavun--Leander--Paar--Yalcin, PRIDE AVR linear-layer optimum
citations.locator: CRYPTO 2014, Sections 5.1-5.2 and Section 6, pp. 12-13 and 17-18

progress.summary: The source reports a 36-cycle PRIDE linear-layer benchmark and asks whether restricting the search to its interleaving construction excludes a better solution.
